newsitem.title: USA: National Semi shares drop on Intel concerns.
newsitem.headline: National Semi shares drop on Intel concerns.

text.p: National Semiconductor Corp shares fell by as much as 18 percent Tuesday in heavy volume after a Morgan Stanley analyst downgraded the stock amid concerns about competition from Intel Corp.
On Monday, Intel unveiled plans for new low priced networking chips aimed at speeding links between workgroup PCs.
Intel may then integrate networking into the motherboards they build, thereby competing with with National's system-on-a-chip product, a key area of growth.
In late trade, National Semiconductor was down 3-1/2 at 23-3/8 and was the NYSE's third most actively traded stock. It hit a low of 21-5/8 earlier.

Morgan Stanley's Dan Myers was not available for comment on his downgrade of National Semicondutor, but analysts familiar with the report said he cut his rating to neutral from outperform, noting that Intel's move posted a "direct competitive threat" to National.
However, they said that he kept intact his earnings estimates for fiscal 1997 and 1998.
Analysts said the sharp share price drop was an overreaction to the report, particularly in light of Myers' unchanged earnings outlook.
"He just said that out on the horizon there is a cloud, and beware of the cloud," which National is capable of doing, said Robert Gutenstein, an analyst for Kalb, Voorhis & Co.
"Give anybody in the semiconductor industry a two-year window and they will turn the company around," he said.

Smith Barney analyst James Barlage, who maintains a buy rating on National, said the Intel's move could shave about two percent off of National's annual revenues, but failed to see it as blow worth such a sharp stock selloff.
"Intel is a powerful company...but I don't know if they will be a more substantial competitor (to National) than anyone else," Barlage said.
